newsitem.title: UK: BASSA strike operational impact Wednesday, July 9.
newsitem.headline: BASSA strike operational impact Wednesday, July 9.

text.p: Industrial action by members of the British Airlines' Stewards and Stewardesses Association (BASSA) has today (Wednesday) forced the cancellation of 135 British Airways' flights from Heathrow and nine services from Gatwick airport
Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Bangkok, Boston, Brisbane, Chicago, Dubai, Durban, Hong Kong, Johannesburg, Los Angeles, Manila, Miami, Muscat, New York, Perth, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo.

Athens (2), Barcelona (2), Berlin (2), Budapest, Copenhagen, Dusseldorf(2), Frankfurt, Gothenburg, Istanbul (2), Larnaca, Lisbon (2), Madrid, Milan (2), Moscow, Munich (2), Nice (2), Oslo, Prague (2), Rome (3), Stockholm (2), Venice, Vienna, Warsaw, Zurich (2).
On a normal day, British Airways would fly 40,000 customers out of Heathrow. The number carried today will be about 14,000 i.e about 35 percent of usual numbers departing.
Dallas/Fort Worth, Miami, Barbados, St Lucia, Pittsburgh, Buenos Aires, Houston, Nairobi and Entebbe.
Atlanta, New York, Lagos, Charlotte, Phoenix, Kingston, Baltimore, Harare, Lusaka, Accra, San Diego and Montego Bay.
On a normal day British Airways would fly 15,000 customers out of Gatwick
The figure will be almost the same today, about 13,800 - i.e. ninety percent of usual numbers travelling.
....The flight schedule for British Airways' services from Heathrow and Gatwick for tomorrow (Thursday, May 10) will be announced later today (Wednesday).
Many flights are operating normally, with cabin crews not involved in the dispute. These include:
All UK domestic flights to and from Gatwick
All European flights to and from Gatwick ....International flights to and from UK regional airports
UK domestic services, other than those serving Heathrow.

All services operated by the airline's franchise and alliance partners - British Regional Airlines, Brymon Airways, Loganair, Maersk Air, GB Airways, CityFlyer Express, TAT/Air , Deutsche BA, Qantas, Comair, Canadian International, America West, Sun Air and British Mediterranean.

....Details of these flights, together with guidance for customers on flights which may be disrupted are being made available through travel agents and British Airways travel shops, on ITV teletext page 380, on the airline's Internet web site www.british-airway.com/strike, and on its special information line, 0800 727 800.
....British Airways World Cargo is providing similar information for the airline's freight customer.
The airline will also continue its newspaper and radio advertising to keep customers informed.

Customers due to fly with British Airways on flights which are not operating will be rebooked onto.other British Airways services on the nearest alternative days, offered a full refund, or, where space is available, transferred on to other airlines.

....Customers who have already started their flights and due to return during the period of the strike on flights which have been cancelled are recommended to make contact with British Airway. They will be transferred on to alternative British Airways' flights, where possible or to other carriers. Or they can have their money back for unused ticket coupons.
